d: Learn everything you need to know about creating on Roblox.
h:
Learn everything you need to know about creating on Roblox.

If you're new to developing Roblox games, read these guides for a tour of Roblox creation before diving into the product documentation and tutorials.

The Roblox platform

Roblox is free-to-use for both users and creators and spans a broad demographic with different user behaviors than other social platforms. Learn what makes Roblox unique and what to think about before creating.

Overview

Learn about our unique platform and values. Learn more

The Roblox user base

Learn what characterizes the Roblox audience, and what social and cultural factors you should consider when developing on the platform. Learn more

Designing for Roblox

Discover some common practices from successful games and find out how to tailor your designs to the unique characteristics of Roblox. Learn more

Games

Games, also referred to as experiences, are the 3D worlds that you create and publish in Roblox. Learn how they technically work, so you understand how to build the best games possible for your users.

Roblox projects

Understand how to build projects in Roblox Studio and publish them as games on Roblox. Learn more

Work with assets

Understand how to upload assets to the Roblox cloud and how to use them in your projects. Learn more

The data model

Understand the data model, the underlying definition of how places in your 3D games look and function. Learn more

Client-server runtime

Understand how your games run in the Roblox Cloud. Learn more

3D workspace

The 3D workspace is where you define all objects that are rendered by Roblox. Learn more

Scripting

Learn how to script logic for your Roblox games. Learn more

Characters

Understand how character models work for NPCs and Players in Roblox. Learn more

Custom models and meshes

Understand how to use Blender and other tools to create custom 3D objects. Learn More

Roblox Studio

Studio is an all-in-one IDE that lets you create on Roblox. You build projects that you can later publish as games to Roblox and also use Studio to create characters and accessories.

Studio overview

Learn about Studio, the all-in-one IDE for Roblox. Learn more

UI overview

Learn about the Studio UI and all the features and tools that are available. Learn more

Discovery and monetization

With tens of millions daily active users, there's many ways to monetize and grow your creations.

Promoting on Roblox

Discover how games are commonly promoted on Roblox and how you can spend your budget most appropriately. Learn more

Earning on Roblox

Learn about monetization options and strategies on the platform along with associated considerations for developers. Learn more

Avatars

Learn how to build character models and accessories in 3rd party tools like Blender and Maya and sell them on the Marketplace. See Avatars for creation guides, technical specifications, and additional resources.

kid.simple: This page is a map of everything you can learn about making things on Roblox. It does not teach one skill. Instead, it points you to the guides for each big topic: the platform and its players, how games work inside, Roblox Studio, getting players and earning Robux, and making avatar items. If you are brand new, start here to see the whole picture before you dive into one area.
kid.analogy: It is like the map at the entrance of a theme park. It does not give you a ride, but it shows you where every ride is so you can pick where to go first.
keyPoints: Roblox is free for both players and creators, and its players behave differently from people on other social apps, so it helps to learn about them first.
Games (also called experiences) are the 3D worlds you build and publish on Roblox.
Under the hood, a game is a project made of places, assets, and settings, and each place is described by something called the data model.
Games run on Roblox's servers in the cloud and on each player's device, which is called the client-server runtime.
Roblox Studio is the free all-in-one program you use to build, script, test, and publish games, and also to make characters and accessories.
There are guides on promoting your game so players find it, and on ways to earn money from it.
You can make avatar items in tools like Blender or Maya and sell them on the Marketplace.

terms.experience: Another name Roblox uses for a game. Both words mean the same thing.
terms.platform: The whole Roblox system: the app, the website, the servers, and all the people using it.
terms.IDE: Short for Integrated Development Environment. It is one program that has everything you need to make something, like building tools, a code editor, and a test button. Roblox Studio is an IDE.
terms.data model: The tree of objects (parts, scripts, folders, and so on) that describes everything in a place. You see it in the Explorer window in Studio.
terms.client-server runtime: How a game actually runs: a Roblox computer in the cloud (the server) runs the official game, and each player's device (a client) shows it and sends their actions.
terms.3D workspace: The part of your game that holds all the things players can see in the 3D world, like parts and models.
terms.monetization: Ways to earn money from your game, such as selling passes or items for Robux.
terms.Marketplace: The Roblox shop where people buy avatar items like hats, clothes, and accessories.
terms.assets: Files your game uses, such as images, sounds, and 3D meshes, stored online by Roblox.

watchOut: Trying to read everything at once. Pick one topic, like Roblox Studio or the first tutorial, and come back to the map later.
Skipping the client-server and data model guides. They explain why scripts sometimes work in one place but not another, which saves lots of confusion later.
